requirement: Describe a prospective, single-center, two-arm randomized 12-month trial in adults with lupus nephritis receiving mycophenolate mofetil, comparing therapeutic-drug-monitoring-guided dose management with standard clinical management.

evidence.text: The protocol describes a randomized clinical trial at HU-UFMA over 12 months comparing TDM-guided MMF with usual management.

requirement: Randomize eligible participants 1:1 in blocks of four using a computer-generated sequence prepared by an independent researcher and conceal assignment in sealed opaque envelopes.

evidence.text: Participants will be randomly assigned 1:1 in blocks of four; an independent researcher generates the sequence and sealed opaque envelopes provide concealment.

requirement: Reconcile the protocol's two simultaneous randomized arms with the registry label sequential assignment, and treat the trial as parallel only after confirming that participants do not cross sequential intervention stages.

evidence.text: The protocol describes 1:1 assignment to concurrent TDM-guided and control groups, while the registry metadata labels the intervention model sequential.

requirement: State exactly who is masked and when unblinding occurs: participants and outcome assessors are registry-listed as masked, data analysts remain blinded until analysis, but treating clinicians and the pharmacist must know TDM recommendations; do not call the whole trial simply double-blind without qualifications.

evidence.text: The protocol says observers and analysts are blinded while pharmacist recommendations are discussed with the treating rheumatologist.

requirement: Use an intention-to-treat primary analysis containing all randomized participants in their assigned TDM-guided or standard-management group.

evidence.text: The primary analysis will be conducted using the intention-to-treat approach.

requirement: Complete the primary treatment-policy estimand by specifying how dose changes, temporary or permanent MMF discontinuation, rescue or nonprotocol therapy, dialysis, transplant, hospitalization and death affect the 12-month renal-remission outcome while retaining randomized assignment.

evidence.text: The protocol anticipates dose adjustment, toxicity, hospitalization and nonresponse but does not define their estimand treatment.
The SAP states ITT without specifying intercurrent-event strategies.

requirement: Define the primary endpoint as the proportion of randomized participants achieving complete or partial renal remission at 12 months, with absence of either category classified as no remission.

evidence.text: The primary outcome is the proportion in renal remission at 12 months, dichotomized as complete or partial remission versus absence of remission.
The SAP compares the proportion achieving renal remission at 12 months.

requirement: Operationalize complete and partial renal remission using mutually exclusive rules for proteinuria or UPCR, serum creatinine and eGFR at the 12-month visit; reconcile the protocol's overlapping 3-, 6- and 6-12-month thresholds before database lock.

evidence.text: The protocol lists several change and threshold rules at 3, 6, 12 and 6-12 months but does not map them unambiguously to complete versus partial remission.

requirement: Compare the unadjusted 12-month renal-remission proportions between randomized groups using a chi-square test, with Fisher's exact test used when expected-cell conditions make chi-square inappropriate.

evidence.text: The proportion achieving renal remission at 12 months will be compared using chi-square or Fisher's exact test as appropriate.

requirement: Fit an adjusted logistic-regression model for 12-month renal remission containing randomized group, age, nephritic-versus-nephrotic syndrome and baseline MMF dose, and report the adjusted treatment odds ratio.

evidence.text: The SAP specifies adjusted logistic regression controlling for age, nephritic and nephrotic syndrome, and baseline MMF dose.

requirement: Prespecify whether the unadjusted chi-square or Fisher comparison or the adjusted logistic-regression treatment effect is the primary confirmatory analysis; label the other supportive and use only the chosen primary result for the study success decision.
acceptable_values: study success bound to primary analysis

evidence.text: The SAP lists an unadjusted proportion test and adjusted logistic regression without specifying their inferential hierarchy.

requirement: Reconcile the protocol's two-sided planning alpha of 0.10 with the SAP's analysis significance level of 0.05, state the confirmatory sidedness and alpha, and explain whether the 95% confidence interval or a 90% interval corresponds to the primary decision rule.

evidence.text: The sample-size calculation assumes alpha 0.10 and 70% power.
The SAP adopts a 5% significance level and 95% confidence intervals.

requirement: Reproduce and correct the prospective sample-size calculation based on 60% versus 80% remission, two groups, alpha 0.10 and 70% power, and reconcile the statement that 49 per group plus up to 10% loss was merely rounded to 50 per group.

evidence.text: The protocol derives 49 participants per group from 60% versus 80%, alpha 0.10 and power 70%, then says up to 10% loss was addressed by rounding to 50.

requirement: Summarize trough MPA concentration at T1, T2 and T5 and compare groups using Student's t test when its assumptions are met or the Mann-Whitney test otherwise.

evidence.text: MPA C0 is measured at T1, T2 and T5 and is a secondary outcome.
MPA concentrations use descriptive statistics and Student's t or Mann-Whitney between-group tests.

requirement: Define the distributional diagnostics and summary statistics that select Student's t test versus Mann-Whitney for MPA concentrations, and state whether repeated T1/T2/T5 values are reduced to one visit-specific contrast or modeled longitudinally.

evidence.text: The SAP offers t or Mann-Whitney tests but gives no selection rule or repeated-measures specification.

requirement: Prespecify analyses for the remaining secondary outcomes: adverse events related to MMF, lupus-nephritis hospitalizations, medication adherence by BMQ, dose adjustments, MMF dose, nonresponse, relapse, discontinuation for toxicity and pharmacist interventions.

evidence.text: The protocol lists these clinical, pharmacotherapeutic and implementation outcomes.
The SAP inventories variables but only specifies tests for remission and MPA concentration.

requirement: Prespecify missing-data handling for the binary 12-month remission endpoint, incomplete laboratory components, absent MPA visits and BMQ data; report missingness by arm and include an ITT-compatible sensitivity analysis rather than silently analyzing complete cases.

evidence.text: The plan lists collected variables and analyses but no missing-data method.

requirement: Define the confirmatory family and multiplicity policy across the primary remission test, adjusted model and secondary clinical, pharmacokinetic, safety and exploratory biomarker outcomes; prevent exploratory p-values from independently establishing trial success.
acceptable_values: multiplicity method or explicit exploratory status

evidence.text: The SAP applies a general 5% level while listing several analyses and potential exploratory models without a multiplicity strategy.

requirement: Define a safety population based on actual MMF or TDM exposure and summarize participant incidence, event counts, severity, seriousness, relatedness, toxicity-driven interruption or discontinuation and deaths by randomized treatment group.

evidence.text: The protocol names MMF adverse events, toxicity contacts and discontinuation outcomes but no safety analysis population or summaries.

requirement: If survival or mixed-effects models are retained, define their endpoint, time origin, event or censoring rules, fixed and random effects, covariance structure and missing-data assumptions before unblinding; otherwise omit them rather than choosing them from observed completeness or volume.

evidence.text: The plan says survival and mixed-effects models may be conducted depending on completeness and volume of the data, without executable specifications.

requirement: State the trial success criterion as a favorable between-group effect on 12-month renal remission under the selected primary analysis at the reconciled alpha, including the required direction and whether the confidence interval must exclude the null.

evidence.text: The objective and power assumptions expect higher remission with TDM but do not define an analysis success rule.
The SAP lists tests and a 5% level without an explicit success criterion.

requirement: Keep the independent three-page SAP annotation-only and outside all model-visible inputs; expose only the six-page protocol when generating a candidate SAP.

evidence.text: The protocol defines design, interventions, sample size and endpoints but not the independent SAP's ITT, tests, regression covariates or software.
The separate plan contains the reference-only inferential methods and software.

requirement: Identify unresolved design, endpoint, alpha, sample-size, masking, missingness and multiplicity choices as confirmation questions rather than inventing decisions unsupported by the short source documents.

evidence.text: The concise protocol contains internal ambiguities and does not specify several executable analysis decisions.
The concise SAP adds several methods but remains incomplete and data-contingent.
